How Long Is the Immigration Queue at Phu Quoc Airport in October 2026?

In October 2026, the last passengers off a flight landing in the busiest hours need an estimated 59–94 minutes from touchdown to leaving immigration at Phu Quoc International Airport (PQC). At quieter hours it is 37–46 minutes. With Fast Track it is about 10 minutes, and under 15 even at the busiest hours.

When Fast Track matters most

Flights landing 16:00–20:00, when arrivals from Hong Kong, Taipei, Bangkok and Singapore land minutes apart. Land 10:00–13:00 and 20:00–24:00 — the line is shorter, though rarely short.

October 2026 notes

1–7 October is China's National Day — extra charters, busier days. From 25 October the winter schedule adds Korean, Russian and Central Asian night flights.

How we estimate: a minute-by-minute queue model over the 25 international arrivals on a typical October weekday, counting deplaning and the walk to the hall, and checked against the waits travellers report. Estimates, not measurements.

What We Offer

What Is Airport Fast Track?

Phu Quoc (PQC) is Vietnam's only visa-free gateway — 30 days, every nationality. But it is a single terminal with few counters: quiet days clear in minutes, three charters at once do not. Fast Track is a licensed airport assistance service that keeps you under 15 minutes, whatever the crowd.

Peak hours — PQC

When the Charters Land

Visa-free still means queueing for the exemption stamp. When two or three charters land in the same hour the counters fill — over an hour at peak, longer at Tet.

Your name. Our sign.

We're Already Waiting

Our assistant is in the arrival hall with your name on a sign. No searching after an overnight flight, no guessing about PAI or the visa-exemption counter.

Priority Lane — PQC

Through in About 10 Minutes

Priority immigration lane, PAI and paperwork handled, escort to the exit. The regular line is still in the hall while you are on your way to the resort.

The Difference

Arrive at your resort calm and rested, the way the holiday should start

FAQ

Frequently Asked Questions

Everything you need to know before booking your Fast Track at Phu Quoc Airport. Still have questions? Chat with us on WhatsApp.

Visa-free doesn't mean queue-free. Phu Quoc grants a 30-day visa exemption to every nationality, but you still line up to have it stamped, and officers may ask for your onward ticket. When several charters land in the same hour at the single terminal, that line builds fast. Fast Track takes you through the priority lane in about 10 minutes, under 15 at peak.

In October 2026, the last passengers off a flight landing in the busiest hours need an estimated 59–94 minutes from touchdown to leaving immigration. At quieter hours it is 37–46 minutes.

With Fast Track it is under 15 minutes even at the busiest hours, and about 10 when the hall is lighter. See the estimate for your landing time (updated 2 October 2026).

Most travelers need only a valid passport — Phu Quoc grants a 30-day visa exemption to all nationalities on a direct arrival. Bring proof of onward or return travel; officers may ask. Staying beyond 30 days or continuing to the mainland, you may also hold:

  • E-Visa (applied online in advance)
  • Visa on Arrival approval letter
  • Temporary Residence Card
  • APEC Business Travel Card

Note: Fast Track is for foreign passport holders only. Vietnamese passport holders use the autogate system.

Yes. Since 1 June 2026 every foreign arrival at Phu Quoc must complete a Pre-Arrival Information (PAI) registration online before landing, at prearrival.immigration.gov.vn, within 72 hours of your flight. You get a QR code to show on arrival.

If you haven't done it, our assistant sorts the PAI on the spot so it doesn't hold you up at the counter.

Fast Track Arrival ([paf_price service="fast_track_arrival"]/person) — our assistant meets you in the arrival hall, takes you through the priority immigration lane, handles your PAI and visa-exemption paperwork, and gets you out in about 10 minutes, under 15 at peak.

Fast Track Departure ([paf_price service="fast_track_departure"]/person) — we meet you at the departures entrance and take you through the priority exit lane, skipping the passport-control queue.

Many guests book both ends of the trip.

No. Our fee covers personal assistance only. Official government fees — Visa on Arrival stamping, for example — are paid directly to the authorities on the day. Most visa-exempt travelers pay nothing extra, and we tell you in advance if a fee applies. There is no ATM inside the immigration area, so bring USD or VND if you expect one.

For arrivals, our assistant waits in the arrival hall with your name on a sign, right before immigration control, then takes you through the priority lane. Phu Quoc has a single terminal — no wrong building to head for.

For departures, we meet you at the departures entrance. We send the exact meeting point after confirmation.

Yes, a $10 surcharge per person applies for night flights. The windows differ slightly between services:

  • Arrivals: between 10:00 PM and 6:00 AM
  • Departures: between 12:00 AM and 8:00 AM

Many Korean, Chinese and Central Asian charters to Phu Quoc land in these hours. Our service is available 24/7 regardless of flight time.

We monitor your flight in real time and adjust. Our assistant is there whether you land early, on time or late.

Yes — solo travelers, couples, families and larger groups. Just tell us the passenger count when booking. For children:

  • Infants under 2 travel free of charge
  • Passengers aged 2 and over pay the full price

Families benefit most — no long queue with tired children after the flight.

We confirm your booking first — no advance payment. You then pay online by PayPal or credit card (no PayPal account needed) through a secure link we send after confirmation. We do not take cash.

Book through the website checkout, WhatsApp or email — send your flight number, date, passenger count and chosen service. We confirm within 10 minutes, day or night.

Many guests book both arrival and departure. Just send both flight details when booking.
